title: Can Productivity Be Reduced to a Score?
titleZh: 生產力能化成一個分數嗎？
summaryZh: 經理與資料分析師討論員工生產力分數的盲點，並設計兼顧決策用途與人性風險的評估方式。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: The board wants a single productivity score for every department by the end of the quarter.
sentences.zh: 董事會希望在本季結束前，為每個部門建立單一生產力分數。

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: A single score is easy to compare, but that convenience may be exactly what makes it dangerous.
sentences.zh: 單一分數很容易比較，但這種便利或許正是它危險的原因。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: They are not asking us to judge individuals, only to see which teams need more support.
sentences.zh: 他們不是要我們評判個人，只是想看哪些團隊需要更多支援。

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: That intention helps, although department metrics have a habit of becoming individual targets later.
sentences.zh: 這個出發點有幫助，不過部門指標往往之後會變成個人目標。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: What would be wrong with combining completed projects, response time, and customer ratings?
sentences.zh: 把完成的專案數、回應時間與客戶評分合在一起，有什麼問題？

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: Those measures reward visible output, while maintenance and careful prevention often remain invisible.
sentences.zh: 那些衡量方式獎勵看得見的產出，但維護與謹慎預防往往是看不見的。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: So the team that prevents a crisis could score lower than the team that fixes one dramatically.
sentences.zh: 所以預防危機的團隊，分數可能比轟轟烈烈解決危機的團隊更低。

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: Exactly, and once people know the formula, they will naturally organize their work around it.
sentences.zh: 正是如此，而且人們一旦知道公式，自然會圍繞它安排工作。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: That does not mean every measurement is useless; we still need evidence for staffing decisions.
sentences.zh: 這不表示所有衡量都沒用，我們在人力決策上仍然需要證據。

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: I agree, but I would present a dashboard of several signals rather than compressing them into one rank.
sentences.zh: 我同意，但我會呈現包含多項訊號的儀表板，而不是把它們壓成單一排名。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: The board will ask how to interpret a dashboard when the signals point in different directions.
sentences.zh: 當不同訊號指向不同方向時，董事會會問該如何解讀儀表板。

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: That disagreement is information, because it tells us where a simple story would hide a tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 那種不一致本身就是資訊，因為它告訴我們簡單說法會在哪裡掩蓋取捨。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: Could we add a written review so teams can explain unusual conditions behind their numbers?
sentences.zh: 我們能否加入書面檢視，讓團隊解釋數字背後的特殊情況？

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: Yes, and we should prevent the data from being used for bonuses until we have tested it for bias.
sentences.zh: 可以，而且在檢驗資料是否有偏誤之前，我們應避免把它用於獎金決定。

sentences.speaker: A
sentences.text: I will propose a six month pilot with department trends, written context, and no employee ranking.
sentences.zh: 我會提議進行六個月試行，觀察部門趨勢、附上書面脈絡，且不做員工排名。

sentences.speaker: B
sentences.text: That gives us something useful to learn from without pretending the score knows more than we do.
sentences.zh: 這樣我們能得到有用的學習材料，也不會假裝分數比我們懂得更多。

questions.q: Why is B concerned about creating one productivity score?
options: It would take too long to calculate
It could hide important work and shape behavior around the formula
It would reveal private customer information

questions.q: What does B suggest using instead of a single rank?
What limits will the proposed pilot include?
options: It will cover only one week of data
It will rank employees but not departments
It will include context and avoid employee ranking
